l.i: Beati Pauli dictum, Scimus idolum nihil esse in mundo, pro Bellarmino nihil facere: nec simile ex apocrypha appendice libri Esther ab Hieronymo citatum.

main_text.l: TErtiò[?], quia B. Paulus 1. Corinth. 8. ait: Scimus, quia nihil est idolum in mundo. Vbi idolum nihil esse dicitur, quia licet sit aliquid secundum materiam, tamen nihil est formaliter, cum id repraesentet quod nihil est, & proinde nec vere repraesentet, & consequenter nec sit. Cui loco alium similem adducit Hieronymus in caput 7. Osea, ad probandum idolum nihil esse; nam Hester 14. secundum LXX. dicitur: Ne tradas sceptrum tuum his, qui non sunt, id est, idolis.

INter varia genera fallacium rationum, quibus sophistæ videntur redarguere convinceréque eos adver-sum quos disputant, revera autem non redarguunt, latissimè patentem (ut observavit {a}Aristoteles) ac principem locum obtinet

page.notes: The large initials are decorated woodcut letters. The first one, before "Ertiò", is read as T (for "Tertiò"), but the letter is uncertain, hence [?]. The second, before "Nter", is read as I. The long s in the printed text and margin notes is set as s. The marginal note "controuers.7." is given as "controuers.7.". The printed text was partly faint at the top margin, where faint show-through of the other page appears and was left out.
